interpretation.diagram_classification: cosmological / natural-philosophical diagram (concentric scheme of the four elements, qualities, seasons and humours, microcosm–macrocosm)
interpretation.interpretation: The diagram is a medieval scheme of correspondences between the macrocosm (mundus), time (annus) and the human being (homo), as named in the central circle. Around this centre, a ring of interlaced bands links the four elements (Ignis, Aer, Aqua, Terra) with the four qualities (Calidus, Siccus, Humidus, Frigidus), the four seasons (Ver, Aestas, Autumnus, Hiems) and the four humours (Sanguis, Colera, Melancholia, Flegma). The interlacing shows that each element shares one quality with the element before it and one with the element after it. Fire is hot and dry, air hot and humid, water humid and cold, earth cold and dry. The wheel thus presents one common fourfold order governing the world, the year and the human body.
interpretation.evidence: Written in the diagram: the central text "MVNDVS. ANNVS. HOMO."; the repeated quality labels "Sicca", "Calidvs", "Humidvs", "Frigida"; the element labels "Ignis", "Aer", "Aqua" and, with the abbreviated reading from Step 1, "Terra"; the humoral terms "Colera", "Sangvis" and "melancho"; the seasonal terms "Ver" and "Hi[em]". Visible: concentric circles and interlaced bands, with the paired quality labels placed between the element labels. External knowledge: this is the standard early medieval fourfold scheme, familiar from Isidore of Seville's De natura rerum and from Bede's computistical works. This identification of the tradition is a general one and I cannot name a specific source for this copy with confidence. Step 1 problems: the transcriptions "Ter ra", "Avt[illegible]" (probably "Aestas" or "Autumnus"), "Hiem[illegible]" and the lower inner arc (probably "Flegma") are uncertain. Entries 16–21 are low-certainty. Several "connected_to" relations in Step 1 between text labels (for example Sicca–Ignis) describe interlaced bands and not necessarily a causal link. The Step 1 reading "Es" near the top may be part of "Aestas", which Step 1 did not record correctly.

interpretation.diagram_classification: microcosm–macrocosm and temporal diagram (world, year, man)
interpretation.interpretation: The central circle "MVNDVS ANNVS HOMO" is the key to the whole scheme. It declares that the world (space and elements), the year (time and seasons) and man (the body and its humours) all share the same structure. The concentric rings each express one of these three domains. The outer ring carries the elements and qualities (world), the middle ring the seasons (year) and the inner ring the humours (man). The three lines in the centre stand for the three parallel orders of reality.
interpretation.evidence: Written: the three words in the central circle, with each ring labelled with terms from one of the three domains. Visible: the concentric arrangement. External: the mundus–annus–homo triad is a well-known medieval formula for the microcosm–macrocosm correspondence. The assignment of particular rings to particular domains rests on partly illegible labels (Step 1 entries 16–21) and so is only medium certain.

interpretation.interpretation: The interlacing of the bands is a diagrammatic device that shows the combination and transition of the paired qualities. Each band, with one quality label, passes over and under the bands of neighbouring qualities, so that adjacent elements are visibly bound together. The repeated labels (two "Calidvs", two "Frigida", two "Sicca", two "Humidvs") mark the quality that is shared by two neighbouring elements. The closed ring suggests the cycle of the seasons and the continuous transformation of the elements into one another.
interpretation.evidence: Visible: red-outlined bands pass over and under each other in a closed ring, with the same quality words repeated on the two adjacent bands. External: the shared qualities of neighbouring elements are standard in the tradition. The significance of the interlacing is my own inference from the form and is not stated in the text. Step 1 entries 2–15 connect these labels but give only low-to-medium certainty on a few of the transitions, such as Calidvs–Aer.
